NKJV.1: Now this is the genealogy of the sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. And sons were born to them after the flood.
NKJV.2: The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
NKJV.3: The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
NKJV.4: The sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
NKJV.5: From these the coastland peoples of the Gentiles were separated into their lands, everyone according to his language, according to their families, into their nations.
NKJV.6: The sons of Ham were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
NKJV.7: The sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabtechah; and the sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
NKJV.8: Cush begot Nimrod; he began to be a mighty one on the earth.
NKJV.9: He was a mighty hunter before the LORD; therefore it is said, “Like Nimrod the mighty hunter before the LORD.”
NKJV.10: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
NKJV.11: From that land he went to Assyria and built Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, Calah,
NKJV.12: and Resen between Nineveh and Calah (that is the principal city).
NKJV.13: Mizraim begot Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
NKJV.14: Pathrusim, and Casluhim (from whom came the Philistines and Caphtorim).
NKJV.15: Canaan begot Sidon his firstborn, and Heth;
NKJV.16: the Jebusite, the Amorite, and the Girgashite;
NKJV.17: the Hivite, the Arkite, and the Sinite;
NKJV.18: the Arvadite, the Zemarite, and the Hamathite. Afterward the families of the Canaanites were dispersed.
NKJV.19: And the border of the Canaanites was from Sidon as you go toward Gerar, as far as Gaza; then as you go toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
NKJV.20: These were the sons of Ham, according to their families, according to their languages, in their lands and in their nations.
NKJV.21: And children were born also to Shem, the father of all the children of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder.
NKJV.22: The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.
NKJV.23: The sons of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
NKJV.24: Arphaxad begot Salah, and Salah begot Eber.
NKJV.25: To Eber were born two sons: the name of one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided; and his brother’s name was Joktan.
NKJV.26: Joktan begot Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
NKJV.29: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
NKJV.30: And their dwelling place was from Mesha as you go toward Sephar, the mountain of the east.
NKJV.31: These were the sons of Shem, according to their families, according to their languages, in their lands, according to their nations.
NKJV.32: These were the families of the sons of Noah, according to their generations, in their nations; and from these the nations were divided on the earth after the flood.

NASB.3: The sons of Gomer [were] Ashkenaz and Riphath and Togarmah.
NASB.4: The sons of Javan [were] Elishah and Tarshish, Kittim and Dodanim.
NASB.5: From these the coastlands of the nations were separated into their lands, every one according to his language, according to their families, into their nations.
NASB.6: The sons of Ham [were] Cush and Mizraim and Put and Canaan.
NASB.7: The sons of Cush [were] Seba and Havilah and Sabtah and Raamah and Sabteca; and the sons of Raamah [were] Sheba and Dedan.
NASB.8: Now Cush became the father of Nimrod; he became a mighty one on the earth.
NASB.9: He was a mighty hunter before the LORD; therefore it is said, 'Like Nimrod a mighty hunter before the LORD.'
NASB.10: The beginning of his kingdom was Babel and Erech and Accad and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
NASB.11: From that land he went forth into Assyria, and built Nineveh and Rehoboth-Ir and Calah,
NASB.12: and Resen between Nineveh and Calah; that is the great city.
NASB.13: Mizraim became the father of Ludim and Anamim and Lehabim and Naphtuhim
NASB.14: and Pathrusim and Casluhim (from which came the Philistines) and Caphtorim.
NASB.15: Canaan became the father of Sidon, his firstborn, and Heth
NASB.16: and the Jebusite and the Amorite and the Girgashite
NASB.17: and the Hivite and the Arkite and the Sinite
NASB.18: and the Arvadite and the Zemarite and the Hamathite; and afterward the families of the Canaanite were spread abroad.
NASB.19: The territory of the Canaanite extended from Sidon as you go toward Gerar, as far as Gaza; as you go toward Sodom and Gomorrah and Admah and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
NASB.20: These are the sons of Ham, according to their families, according to their languages, by their lands, by their nations.
NASB.21: Also to Shem, the father of all the children of Eber, [and] the older brother of Japheth, children were born.
NASB.22: The sons of Shem [were] Elam and Asshur and Arpachshad and Lud and Aram.
NASB.23: The sons of Aram [were] Uz and Hul and Gether and Mash.
NASB.24: Arpachshad became the father of Shelah; and Shelah became the father of Eber.
NASB.25: Two sons were born to Eber; the name of the one [was] Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided; and his brother's name [was] Joktan.
NASB.26: Joktan became the father of Almodad and Sheleph and Hazarmaveth and Jerah
NASB.27: and Hadoram and Uzal and Diklah
NASB.28: and Obal and Abimael and Sheba
NASB.29: and Ophir and Havilah and Jobab; all these were the sons of Joktan.
NASB.30: Now their settlement extended from Mesha as you go toward Sephar, the hill country of the east.
NASB.31: These are the sons of Shem, according to their families, according to their languages, by their lands, according to their nations.
NASB.32: These are the families of the sons of Noah, according to their genealogies, by their nations; and out of these the nations were separated on the earth after the flood.

NLT.1: This is the account of the families of Shem, Ham, and Japheth, the three sons of Noah. Many children were born to them after the great flood.
NLT.2: The descendants of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
NLT.3: The descendants of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
NLT.4: The descendants of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
NLT.5: Their descendants became the seafaring peoples that spread out to various lands, each identified by its own language, clan, and national identity.
NLT.6: The descendants of Ham were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
NLT.7: The descendants of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The descendants of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
NLT.8: Cush was also the ancestor of Nimrod, who was the first heroic warrior on earth.
NLT.9: Since he was the greatest hunter in the world, his name became proverbial. People would say, “This man is like Nimrod, the greatest hunter in the world.”
NLT.10: He built his kingdom in the land of Babylonia, with the cities of Babylon, Erech, Akkad, and Calneh.
NLT.11: From there he expanded his territory to Assyria, building the cities of Nineveh, Rehoboth-ir, Calah,
NLT.12: and Resen (the great city located between Nineveh and Calah).
NLT.13: Mizraim was the ancestor of the Ludites, Anamites, Lehabites, Naphtuhites,
NLT.14: Pathrusites, Casluhites, and the Caphtorites, from whom the Philistines came.
NLT.15: Canaan’s oldest son was Sidon, the ancestor of the Sidonians. Canaan was also the ancestor of the Hittites,
NLT.18: Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites. The Canaanite clans eventually spread out,
NLT.19: and the territory of Canaan extended from Sidon in the north to Gerar and Gaza in the south, and east as far as Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, near Lasha.
NLT.20: These were the descendants of Ham, identified by clan, language, territory, and national identity.
NLT.21: Sons were also born to Shem, the older brother of Japheth. Shem was the ancestor of all the descendants of Eber.
NLT.22: The descendants of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.
NLT.23: The descendants of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
NLT.24: Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.
NLT.25: Eber had two sons. The first was named Peleg (which means “division”), for during his lifetime the people of the world were divided into different language groups. His brother’s name was Joktan.
NLT.26: Joktan was the ancestor of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
NLT.29: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were descendants of Joktan.
NLT.30: The territory they occupied extended from Mesha all the way to Sephar in the eastern mountains.
NLT.31: These were the descendants of Shem, identified by clan, language, territory, and national identity.
NLT.32: These are the clans that descended from Noah’s sons, arranged by nation according to their lines of descent. All the nations of the earth descended from these clans after the great flood.

WEB.1: Now this is the history of the generations of the sons of Noah and of Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.
WEB.2: The sons of Japheth were: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
WEB.3: The sons of Gomer were: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
WEB.4: The sons of Javan were: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
WEB.5: Of these were the islands of the nations divided in their lands, everyone after his language, after their families, in their nations.
WEB.6: The sons of Ham were: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
WEB.7: The sons of Cush were: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were: Sheba and Dedan.
WEB.8: Cush became the father of Nimrod. He began to be a mighty one in the earth.
WEB.9: He was a mighty hunter before Yahweh. Therefore it is said, “like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before Yahweh”.
WEB.10: The beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
WEB.11: Out of that land he went into Assyria, and built Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, Calah,
WEB.12: and Resen between Nineveh and the great city Calah.
WEB.13: Mizraim became the father of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
WEB.14: Pathrusim, Casluhim (which the Philistines descended from), and Caphtorim.
WEB.15: Canaan became the father of Sidon (his firstborn), Heth,
WEB.16: the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
WEB.17: the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
WEB.18: the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Afterward the families of the Canaanites were spread abroad.
WEB.19: The border of the Canaanites was from Sidon — as you go toward Gerar — to Gaza — as you go toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim — to Lasha.
WEB.20: These are the sons of Ham, after their families, according to their languages, in their lands and their nations.
WEB.21: Children were also born to Shem, the father of all the children of Eber, the elder brother of Japheth.
WEB.22: The sons of Shem were: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
WEB.23: The sons of Aram were: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
WEB.24: Arpachshad became the father of Shelah. Shelah became the father of Eber.
WEB.25: To Eber were born two sons. The name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided. His brother’s name was Joktan.
WEB.26: Joktan became the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
WEB.29: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
WEB.30: Their dwelling extended from Mesha, as you go toward Sephar, the mountain of the east.
WEB.31: These are the sons of Shem, by their families, according to their languages, lands, and nations.
WEB.32: These are the families of the sons of Noah, by their generations, according to their nations. The nations divided from these in the earth after the flood.

CSB17.1: These are the family records <sup>ⓔ</sup> of Noah’s sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth. They also had sons after the flood.
CSB17.2: Japheth’s sons: <sup>ⓕ</sup> Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
CSB17.3: Gomer’s sons: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
CSB17.4: And Javan’s sons: Elishah, Tarshish, <sup>ⓖ</sup> Kittim, and Dodanim. <sup>[1]</sup>
CSB17.5: From these descendants, the peoples of the coasts and islands spread out into their lands according to their clans in their nations, each with its own language.
CSB17.6: Ham’s sons: <sup>ⓗ</sup> Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
CSB17.7: Cush’s sons: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. And Raamah’s sons: Sheba and Dedan.
CSB17.8: Cush fathered Nimrod, who began to be powerful in the land.
CSB17.9: He was a powerful hunter in the sight of the LORD. That is why it is said, “Like Nimrod, a powerful hunter in the sight of the LORD.”
CSB17.10: His kingdom started with Babylon, <sup>ⓘ</sup> Erech, <sup>[2]</sup> Accad, <sup>[3]</sup> and Calneh, <sup>[4]</sup> in the land of Shinar. <sup>[5]</sup> <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.11: From that land he went to Assyria <sup>ⓚ</sup> and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-ir, Calah,
CSB17.12: and Resen, between Nineveh and the great city Calah.
CSB17.13: Mizraim <sup>[6]</sup> <sup>ⓛ</sup> fathered the people of Lud, Anam, Lehab, Naphtuh,
CSB17.14: Pathrus, Casluh (the Philistines came from them), and Caphtor. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.15: Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn and Heth,
CSB17.16: as well as the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites, <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.17: the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
CSB17.18: the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Afterward the Canaanite clans scattered.

CSB17.20: These are Ham’s sons by their clans, according to their languages, in their lands and their nations.
CSB17.21: And Shem, Japheth’s older brother, also had sons. Shem was the father of all the sons of Eber. <sup>ⓐ</sup>

AMP.1: These are the records of the generations (descendants) of Shem, Ham, and Japheth, the sons of Noah; and the sons born to them after the flood:
AMP.2: the sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras;
AMP.3: the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah;
AMP.4: the sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
AMP.5: From these, [the people of] the coastlands of the nations were separated and spread into their lands, every one according to his own language, according to their constituent groups (families), and into their nations:
AMP.6: the sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim [from whom descended the Egyptians], Put, and Canaan;
AMP.7: the sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca; and the sons of Raamah; Sheba and Dedan.
AMP.8: Cush became the father of Nimrod; he became a mighty one on the earth.
AMP.9: He was a mighty hunter before the LORD; therefore it is said, "Like Nimrod a mighty hunter before the LORD."
AMP.10: The beginning of his kingdom was Babel and Erech and Accad and Calneh, in the land of Shinar [in Babylonia].
AMP.11: From that land Nimrod went to Assyria, and built Nineveh, and Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah,
AMP.12: and [Nimrod built] Resen, which is between Nineveh and Calah; all these [combined to form] the great city [Nineveh].
AMP.13: Mizraim [the ancestor of the Egyptians] became the father of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim
AMP.14: and Pathrusim and Casluhim—from whom came the Philistines—and Caphtorim.
AMP.15: Canaan became the father of Sidon, his firstborn, and Heth
AMP.16: and the Jebusite and the Amorite and the Girgashite
AMP.17: and the Hivite and the Arkite and the Sinite
AMP.18: and the Arvadite and the Zemarite and the Hamathite. Afterward the families of the Canaanite were spread abroad.
AMP.19: The territory of the Canaanite extended from Sidon as one goes to Gerar, as far as Gaza; and as one goes to Sodom and Gomorrah and Admah and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
AMP.20: These are the descendants of Ham according to their constituent groups, according to their languages, by their lands, and by their nations.
AMP.21: Also to Shem, the father of all the children of Eber [including the Hebrews], the older brother of Japheth, children were born.
AMP.22: The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud and Aram;
AMP.23: the sons of Aram [ancestor of the Syrians]: Uz, Hul, Gether and Mash.
AMP.24: Arpachshad became the father of Shelah; and Shelah became the father of Eber.
AMP.25: Two sons were born to Eber; the name of one was Peleg (division), for [the inhabitants of] the earth were divided in his days; and his brother's name was Joktan.
AMP.26: Joktan became the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
AMP.29: and Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab; all these were the sons of Joktan.
AMP.30: Now their territory extended from Mesha as one goes toward Sephar, to the hill country of the east.
AMP.31: These are Shem's descendants according to their constituent groups (families), according to their languages, by their lands, according to their nations.
AMP.32: These are the families of the sons of Noah, according to their descendants, by their nations; and from these [people] the nations were separated and spread abroad on the earth after the flood.
